whatFailed: The scenario's only step, the navigation to /reference-host/ooo-note?month=2027-03, never reached DOMContentLoaded inside the harness's fixed 10 second web-step budget (it was still open at 14.7 s), so page.goto threw and the assertion about the publicly shown out-of-office note was never evaluated.

docClaim.quote: (Optional) Add **notes** describing your absence. By default notes are private; toggle **Show notes publicly** if you want bookers to see them on your page.

observed: No product response was ever asserted on. invocation.json records the step as durationMs 14679 with exitCode null and the harness-level timedOut false, i.e. page.goto blew its own 10 s budget rather than the process being killed. The page did get served: four console lines were captured, the same set that passing booking-page scenarios log (markdownToSafeHTML client-side warning, the zustand deprecation, the react-i18next warning, and 'QuickAvailabilityCheck feature enabled: false'), except that loaded siblings log the QuickAvailabilityCheck line TWICE and this run captured it once, which is the app caught mid-hydration. step-1.png is a uniform #efeef3 canvas, the app's own muted page background, so the document shell and its CSS arrived and painted but no content rendered. I extracted frames from session.webm with ffmpeg (17.72 s, 1280x800, 26.8 KB): every sampled frame from 0 s to the end is that same blank background, so unlike the 'renders seconds after the deadline' cases there is no post-deadline frame here (for contrast, the sibling scenario that did render has a 467 KB video). server.stdout/stderr are 0 bytes, which for web scenarios in this run means nothing was captured, not that the server was silent.
impact: None to users. The cost is a lost verdict: this is the only scenario in the corpus that exercises the 'Show notes publicly' half of the out-of-office doc claim, and the run proves nothing about it either way.

fixedAfter.note: Nothing to fix for the timeout itself, it is sandbox timing. For the defect this scenario would have hit had it loaded (see notes): in cal.diy, not fixed. Only 4 commits landed on calcom/cal.diy main between the tested 038381aeca (2026-07-31) and the fetched head 176037d0af (2026-08-08), and `git log 038381aeca..origin/main -- packages/features/availability/lib/getUserAvailability.ts packages/features/schedules/lib/slots.ts packages/features/calendars/components/DatePicker.tsx` is empty, so the whole OOO render path is byte-identical to what was tested. In cal.com: not verifiable from source, the commercial tree is private and the public calcom/cal.com main is a mirror of cal.diy main; my three searches surfaced no public issue, PR or changelog entry.

colleagueFinding.note: This failure belongs to the same flow family as the researcher's finding #1 ('Vacation doesn't stop bookings'), but it did not itself demonstrate it: the page never loaded, so my verdict is environment, not real-defect. Where I refine #1: the researcher frames the trigger as 'if their calendar gets its availability from specific dates rather than a repeating weekly schedule', and I can show from this run's own evidence that the trigger is not exotic, it is how the ENTIRE cal.diy guard corpus is seeded, which is why the OOO family fails wholesale. See notes for the proof and for the answer to 'would this scenario have hit the defect'. I agree with the sibling reviewer's localisation (getUserAvailability.ts:744-755) and independently reached the same blame, PR #13621 'feat: ooo-v2' (880ba8f1dd, 2024-04-09), via `git log --follow -S flattenDays`; the tested-tree blame points at 26b4385679 (2025-12-11, PR #25471 'Add public OOO notes display on booking pages') only because of file moves, though it is worth noting that #25471 is the PR that added the very public-note rendering this scenario asserts on, on top of the already broken filter.

notes:
WHICH SATURATION SIGNATURE. Signature (a) of the two named in the brief, plain first-wave saturation, not the empty-month auto-advance double fetch: the URL carries ?month=2027-03 and March 2027 has a bookable day, so DatePicker never runs its move-to-next-month path. Wave membership is exact: the run started 10:49:00.307Z and the transcript mtimes cluster 03:49:24 to 03:49:49 local for 17 web scenarios, then a gap to 03:50:05 for the next wave. All THREE error outcomes in the run land inside that first cluster (this one and a-dynamic-group-link at 03:49:37, a-public-holiday at 03:49:39) and every later navigation to the same /[user]/[type] route succeeded, including the near-identical /reference-host/ooo-consult booking page 3 seconds earlier in the same wave. Nothing in the evidence points at this route being slow by itself: the app served HTML and CSS, the client bundle booted, and the only thing missing at the deadline was the data-dependent content, which is what a 3-connection Prisma pool under about 16 concurrent workers produces. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: re-run this one scenario alone against an already-warm server, or with concurrency 1, or with the web step budget raised to 30 s; if it renders, environment is proven and the assertion gets a real verdict.

WOULD IT HAVE HIT THE DEFECT? Yes, almost certainly, and it would have failed for that reason rather than passing. Three links, each checked in the tested tree.
(1) The precondition holds for this event type's host. getUserAvailability.ts:744-755 skips an OOO day unless the weekday number appears in flattenDays, the union of `days` over the schedule's availability rows; date-override rows carry a date and an empty days array, so a date-override-only schedule yields flattenDays = [] and every OOO day is dropped. That the reference-host schedules ARE date-override-only is provable from this run without the seed script: DatePicker.tsx:285-311 (useHandleInitialDateSelection) auto-selects the FIRST non-disabled day of the browsed month, and both /reference-host/interval-default?month=2027-03 and /reference-host/default-form?month=2027-03 landed on Mon 15 with no date param in the URL, listing 9:00am to 4:30pm. Under a weekly Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00 schedule the first bookable day of March 2027 would be Monday March 1 (verified: 2027-03-01 is a Monday), so the ten weekdays before the 15th were all disabled, which a weekly schedule cannot produce. The same pattern holds elsewhere in the corpus: /reference-host/split-day and /reference-host/override-check auto-advanced to 2026-09 and selected the 15th, and the override-check scenario's own note says 'the seeded schedule closes the whole run month and opens only the named days of the month after it'. The ooo-consult sibling landed on Wed 12 in June 2030 for the same reason. So the seed pins days with date overrides on a schedule with no weekly rows, which is exactly the shape that empties flattenDays.
(2) The assertion is satisfiable when the OOO IS honored, so the scenario is well formed. With a non-empty flattenDays the entry would mark 2027-03-15 out of office; slots.ts:188-221 stamps every slot of an OOO date with away: true and, when `notes && showNotePublicly`, carries the note; useNonEmptyScheduleDays.ts:13 keeps an away day that has showNotePublicly, so it stays in includedDates; DatePicker.tsx:269-270 computes oooIsSelectable = toUser || showNotePublicly, so a PUBLIC-note OOO day is left enabled (unlike the private-note parent scenario, where the day is disabled); the auto-selection then picks it and AvailableTimes.tsx:305-325 renders OutOfOfficeInSlots.tsx:67-71, which prints the note text verbatim into the page. 'Away at the Cal.com offsite' would therefore be in the page text without any click. This is the only surface in the product where that doc sentence is observable.
(3) With the code as shipped, the page would instead have looked exactly like interval-default: the 15th selectable, 9:00am onward bookable, no emoji, no note, and the step's text assertion would have failed. So the honest expected outcome of a warm re-run is a FAIL that maps onto finding #1, not a pass.
Residual uncertainty, stated plainly: I could not read the seeded rows. reference/seed/guard-seed.mjs is referenced by recipe.json but is absent from the repo and from both scratch clones, and the sandbox Postgres on localhost:5450 is down, so I cannot prove that the ooo-note event type's schedule is date-override-only rather than, say, a weekly schedule fenced by a periodType RANGE, nor that the OutOfOfficeEntry row with showNotePublicly = true was actually inserted. Under the RANGE reading the OOO would be honored and the scenario would pass. I rate that unlikely (it would require the seed to use two different day-pinning mechanisms and the sibling ooo-consult failure to have some other cause), which is why I call it 'almost certainly' rather than certain. A single query settles it: SELECT a.date, a.days, a."startTime", a."endTime" FROM "Availability" a JOIN "Schedule" s ON s.id = a."scheduleId" JOIN users u ON u.id = s."userId" WHERE u.username = 'reference-host', alongside SELECT * FROM "OutOfOfficeEntry" for the same user.

FOR THE HARNESS. Two cheap fixes remove this class of error: warm one booking page after the web health check passes (the gate is /api/auth/csrf, which answers long before any Next route has compiled or touched the DB), and raise the recipe's connection_limit=3 when worker concurrency is above 3. The 10 s budget itself is DEFAULT_WEB_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS in packages/guard-runner/src/web/executor.ts and covers page.goto as well as the assertion.
